transcript.text: Hi everyone, thanks for being here. As we plan the recording evening for preserving our older relatives' stories, I'd like to hear from each of you individually. Nina, could you start by sharing any preferences, advice, or constraints you have regarding the recording and how the files should be handled afterward?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share something important. My grandmother told me she's willing to be recorded only if the interviews stay in the family archive and are not posted publicly online. I haven't had a chance to relay this to anyone yet, but I think this is really important for us to consider as we plan the recording evening and decide how the files will be handled.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I also have something important to share. A friend of mine who works as an audiovisual archivist gave me some specific advice for preserving these recordings. He recommended that the audio should be captured as uncompressed WAV files at exactly 48 kHz and 24-bit depth, and that we should make two verified backup copies of everything. I think this is worth incorporating into our plan to make sure the recordings are properly preserved for future family members.
transcript.speaker: A3
